people.child: Dirty runoff water can make streams unsafe to splash in.
people.adult: Runoff can carry germs and chemicals, so it is wise to avoid direct contact with the water.
people.scientist: Runoff can introduce pathogens, nutrients, and contaminants that affect recreational water safety.

pets.child: Pets should not drink from murky water.
pets.adult: Keep dogs from drinking or swimming in murky stream water.
pets.scientist: Companion animals face exposure risk from contaminated surface water, including algal toxins and pathogens.

wildlife.child: Fewer bugs means less food for birds and frogs.
wildlife.adult: Fewer insects can mean less food for fish, frogs, and birds.
wildlife.scientist: Declining macroinvertebrate diversity can reduce prey availability for higher trophic levels.

environment.child: Rain washes dirt and trash from streets into the stream.
environment.adult: Rain can wash soil, oil, and litter from streets and lots into the stream.
environment.scientist: Stormwater can transport sediment and pollutants that raise turbidity and degrade habitat.

people.child: Trash on the bank can hurt people who walk there.
people.adult: Litter along the bank can create hazards and may point to wider dumping.
people.scientist: Increasing litter can indicate illegal dumping or poor stormwater capture.

pets.child: Pets can get hurt by sharp trash.
pets.adult: Pets can be injured or made sick by broken glass and plastic.
pets.scientist: Companion animals may ingest or be injured by debris.

wildlife.child: Birds can get tangled in plastic.
wildlife.adult: Birds and small animals can swallow or get tangled in plastic.
wildlife.scientist: Plastic debris poses entanglement and ingestion risks to wildlife.

environment.child: Trash can slowly break into tiny pieces.
environment.adult: Plastic can break into tiny pieces that stay in the water.
environment.scientist: Macroplastic fragments into microplastics that persist in sediments.

people.child: A bad smell can mean the water is not clean.
people.adult: A sewage or chemical smell can signal contamination, so keep clear of the water.
people.scientist: Sewage or chemical odors can indicate contamination and warrant sampling.

pets.child: Pets should stay away from smelly water.
pets.adult: Keep pets away from water that smells off.
pets.scientist: Odorous water may carry pathogens or toxicants hazardous to animals.

wildlife.child: Smelly water can be hard for fish to live in.
wildlife.adult: Poor water quality can stress fish and other water life.
wildlife.scientist: Contamination can lower dissolved oxygen and stress aquatic organisms.

environment.child: Something may be leaking into the stream.
environment.adult: A leak or overflow upstream may be adding pollution.
environment.scientist: Odors may indicate point-source discharge or organic loading.

people.child: Fewer kinds of animals can mean the stream is unwell.
people.adult: Few species can signal that the stream is under stress, which affects the places we enjoy.
people.scientist: Low richness is a common indicator of degraded ecological condition.

pets.child: A stream with little life may not be a good place to play.
pets.adult: A stressed stream may be a less safe place for pets to cool off.
pets.scientist: Reduced biological integrity may coincide with higher contaminant exposure.

wildlife.child: Birds and frogs need bugs and little fish to eat.
wildlife.adult: Birds, frogs, and fish rely on a variety of insects and small animals.
wildlife.scientist: Reduced diversity can compromise food web stability.

environment.child: A healthy stream has lots of different small animals.
environment.adult: A healthy stream usually has many kinds of small creatures.
environment.scientist: Sensitive taxa are often lost first under pollution stress.

people.child: We need more people to look at this stream.
people.adult: More volunteer visits would make this picture more reliable.
people.scientist: Small sample sizes limit inference and widen uncertainty.

pets.child: Be careful until we know more.
pets.adult: Until more data arrives, treat conditions as uncertain.
pets.scientist: Sparse data limits risk characterization for companion animals.

wildlife.child: More looks help us spot problems early.
wildlife.adult: More observations help spot changes that affect wildlife early.
wildlife.scientist: Additional observations are needed to detect trends in wildlife indicators.

environment.child: You can help by adding a check.
environment.adult: Adding an observation helps build a clearer picture.
environment.scientist: Increasing observation frequency improves temporal resolution.
